title: Predictive saturation probes and graceful degradation policy for VPC token pipelines
creator: Miguel Santos
description:
Problem: Private VPC deployments sometimes experience sudden token-pipeline saturation (GPU queue growth / KV-cache pressure) that causes downstream latency spikes and increased error rates. Current probes are reactive and surface issues after customer impact. We need a predictive, IaC-delivered probe set that detects approaching saturation and triggers graceful degradation (token shedding + fallback routing) before SLOs are violated.

Goal: Implement Terraform/IaC changes and runtime probe hooks that provide: 1) proactive saturation detection for token throughput and GPU/KV cache pressure, 2) a graded graceful degradation policy (shed non-critical work, route to lower-cost model variants, enable conservative batching), and 3) observability and runbook integration so SREs can validate canary safety and rollback. The work must be deployable via our existing private Terraform modules and compatible with Dedicated fallbacks and Console rollout controls.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic saturation probe detects token pipeline saturation (>=80% token window utilization) within 5 minutes of occurrence in staging with >=90% precision on replayed incidents

When saturation triggers, the system executes the graceful-degradation policy (shed low-priority routes and enable fallback model variant) within 30s and reduces p99 tail latency by at least 30% during the event
Terraform module exposes config knobs: token_window_size, saturation_high_watermark, grace_shed_policy, fallback_model_map and can be applied with zero-downtime for existing VPC stacks
Console surfaces new SLO probe metrics and a dedicated dashboard; alerting rules created for SEV thresholds and a verification playbook linked
Automated canary rollout (Terraform + Console) executes on a small subset of private workers and proves no elevated error rate or latency regressions for 1 hour before full rollout
design_summary: We will extend the VPC health exporter and add a lightweight synthetic token probe sidecar that emits rolling-window token-throughput and cache hit/miss metrics. Probes run two modes: passive (observe real traffic) and active (light synthetic traffic at controlled qps). Detection logic: a moving-window estimator (60s/5m windows) computes token utilization and variance; if utilization crosses saturation_high_watermark and variance indicates queuing growth, emit a predictive_saturation_alert. The graceful degradation controller subscribes to these alerts and performs staged actions: 1) apply per-route shedding rules (configurable percentages), 2) flip routing policies to fallback_model_map for non-critical routes, 3) switch autoscaler to conservative mode. All control surfaces are plumbed through Terraform variables and Console feature gates. We will avoid aggressive shedding for critical customer routes by honoring route-level priority tags.\nOperational safeguards: rate-limit probe-generated requests, circuit-breaker timer to avoid flapping, and a rollback hook to re-enable normal policy after a configurable cool-down.\nSecurity note: probes use internal service account tokens and KMS-protected secrets stored in the VPC module. No customer data is used in synthetic payloads.
rollout_plan: Branch + design doc in Confluence (link below) -> review with SRE and Runtime
Build Terraform changes: new module vars and a 'saturation_probe' submodule; unit tests for plan/diff
Implement probe sidecar and controller in runtime repo; feature gated behind 'vpc_saturation_probes' flag
Deploy to staging VPC stack with synthetic workloads; run incident replay tests
Create Console dashboard & alerting; attach playbook
Canary deploy to 10% of private workers for 1 hour; monitor metrics and rollback on SLO regressions
Full rollout with gradual ramp and post-deploy validation (24h smoke + automated canary checks)
implementation_tasks: TF-Module: add saturation_probe submodule, variables, outputs, and example usage
Runtime: implement probe sidecar (lightweight Go service) emitting prometheus metrics and health endpoints
Controller: implement graceful-degradation controller that consumes alerts and mutates routing via Console API
E2E: add incident replay harness that can simulate token deltas and KV cache pressure
Observability: dashboard panels, SLO probe exporter, and Prometheus alert rules
Docs: runbook update, README for module usage, and PRD link in Confluence
Tests: terraform plan/integration tests; unit tests for controller decisions
